title: What is Bash? 💡
description: Understand what a shell is, why Bash rules, and how you’ll talk to your computer.

slides.title: Shell: Your Command Interpreter 🐚
slides.content:
# The Shell

Imagine your computer as a big building. The **shell** is the receptionist that takes your spoken commands and turns them into actions that the building's workers (the operating system) can execute.

- A shell is a program that interprets commands.
- It reads what you type and sends instructions to the kernel.
- Without a shell, you'd have to program every little task manually.

quizData.question: What is the primary job of a shell?

options.text: To interpret user commands and pass them to the OS
To display images on the screen

quizData.explanation: The shell acts as a command interpreter, bridging the user and the operating system kernel.

slides.title: Bash = Bourne Again SHell 🐧
slides.content:
## Why Bash?

- **Bash** is the most popular shell on Linux and macOS.
- It's an improved version of the original Bourne shell (`sh`).
- Almost every script you see online is written in Bash.
- It's the default shell on most systems – open a terminal and you're likely using Bash!

*Fun fact*: Bash stands for **B**ourne **A**gain **SH**ell, a pun on the original Bourne shell.

quizData.question: Bash is the only shell available on Linux.
quizData.explanation: There are many shells (zsh, fish, ksh, etc.). Bash is just the most common.

slides.title: Graphical vs. Command Line 🖥️ vs ⌨️
slides.content:
## GUI vs CLI

- **GUI (Graphical User Interface)** – clicking icons, dragging files. Easy but limited.
- **CLI (Command Line Interface)** – typing text commands. Fast, powerful, automatable.

Bash lives in the CLI. You tell it exactly what to do, and it does it instantly. No mouse required!

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## The Terminal is Your Friend

Don't be scared of the black screen! Every expert was once a beginner. Start small, and soon you'll feel like a hacker from a movie.
